summary: The audit checks the 60 units: GERMAN 116 (also the WIM course) and GERMAN 191 (the capstone), then electives from GERMAN courses at the 100 or 200 level, GERLANG courses, and ESF or SLE courses (ESF, SLE and COLLEGE together count for at most 10 units). Courses must be letter graded unless offered S/NC only, and at most 10 S/NC units count. The German and Philosophy subplan is optional; with it the major is 65 units, it adds GERMAN 181, PHIL 80, a PHIL 170-series and a PHIL 180-series course and one of three capstones (the honors thesis option uses the same 9 units of DLCL 189H as honors), and up to 10 PHIL units may be CR/NC. Checked by hand: the OPI, electives from Bing Overseas Berlin, IntroSems, COLLEGE or other fields, the subplan's history of philosophy course and two electives, AP units (at most 10, with approval), and the honors thesis and colloquium.

U6FfvZwn.why: The major is 60 units (Minimum Units in the Program); the core courses leave the rest to electives: "Coursework within the department. Additional GERMAN courses at the 100- or 200- level." "Language coursework. All GERLANG courses from the Language Center may be counted." "Education as Self-Fashioning (ESF), Structured Liberal Education (SLE), relevant IntroSems or COLLEGE courses may contribute a maximum of ten units" (a program cap). Bing Overseas Berlin needs the Director of Undergraduate Studies' prior approval, and courses from other fields, relevant IntroSems and COLLEGE courses need a judgment, so they are moved in by hand. Grading: "All courses must be taken for a letter grade unless only offered for a faculty-elected S/NC."

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.desc: To earn honors, students must complete a minimum of 9 units (3 units per quarter), submit a thesis, and present at the Honors Colloquium at the end of their senior year.

children.name: 5,000-word Topic Paper
children.desc:
The student will write a 5,000-word paper on a topic of their choosing, serving as the culmination of their work in the field.
To write the paper, students must enroll in a 3-unit, letter-grade independent study with a faculty member (or affiliate) in the Philosophy and Literature Focal Group. The paper must involve philosophy and literature, and the faculty member must approve the topic by the add/drop deadline.
